name: Hazelden Betty Ford
one_liner: Nonprofit addiction treatment, from virtual outpatient care to residential rehab, combining Twelve Step work with medical care and medication.
best_for: Adults with alcohol or drug addiction who want a structured program
People who need residential treatment or medically managed withdrawal
People with opioid use disorder who want medication (buprenorphine or naltrexone) within a Twelve Step program
Families who want a family program alongside a loved one's treatment
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose danger right now: call 911 or call/text 988
People on Medicare or most Medicaid plans (not accepted, apart from some HealthPartners Medicaid plans in Minnesota)
People who want a program without any Twelve Step component
short_description: Hazelden Betty Ford runs addiction treatment centers in several states and virtual programs in some, mostly paid through private insurance.
long_description: The Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation is a US nonprofit that treats alcohol and drug addiction and related mental health conditions. It offers withdrawal management, residential treatment at centers in Minnesota, California, Oregon and Florida, intensive and standard outpatient programs, virtual (telehealth) outpatient care in some states, family programs and recovery support. Its COR-12 program combines medication for opioid use disorder with Twelve Step-based therapy. It is in network with many commercial insurers but does not take Medicare or most Medicaid plans, and it does not publish program prices; limited financial assistance is available. Its outcome figures are mostly its own patient surveys; one peer-reviewed uncontrolled study describes its opioid program.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; self-pay prices not published
pricing.notes: Cost depends on level of care and your plan. In network with many commercial insurers; Medicare and most Medicaid not accepted (exception: some HealthPartners Medicaid plans in Minnesota). Limited patient financial assistance.

privacy.notes: Patient records fall under HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2; the website policy says it does not sell data but offers an opt-out of targeted advertising and honors GPC for ad sharing.

faqs.q: How much does Hazelden Betty Ford cost?
faqs.a: Costs vary significantly by program level. Residential treatment can be $30,000+ per month, while virtual and outpatient programs are much more affordable. Many insurance plans cover Hazelden Betty Ford at various levels of care.

faqs.q: Does Hazelden Betty Ford use 12-Step programs?
faqs.a: Yes, Hazelden Betty Ford integrates 12-Step principles with evidence-based clinical treatment. This includes introducing patients to AA/NA while also providing medical care, therapy, and MAT when appropriate.

faqs.q: What levels of care does Hazelden Betty Ford offer?
faqs.a: They offer medical detox, residential treatment, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient, outpatient, and virtual programs. Patients step through levels as appropriate for their recovery stage.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover Hazelden Betty Ford?
faqs.a: Many insurance plans cover treatment at Hazelden Betty Ford. Coverage varies by plan and level of care. Their admissions team helps verify benefits and explore coverage options.

patient_summary: Hazelden Betty Ford treats alcohol and drug addiction, from virtual outpatient groups to residential rehab. You start by calling admissions or checking your insurance online, and they recommend a level of care. Most people pay through private insurance; prices are not published and Medicare and most Medicaid plans are not accepted.

availability.note: Residential centers in MN, CA, OR and FL plus outpatient sites; virtual care only in some states. Does not take Medicare or most Medicaid.
